events.say: Attention prisoners. Line up silently in the middle of the yard. We will begin the count.
Prisoners, attention. Line up again. We will begin the count.
Silence! Let's start this count properly.
Silence! Make sure we stick to the rules.
Silence! Maintain order at all times.
Silence! Let's get to work without any further delay.
Silence! Prepare for the evening count. Let's end today on a good note.
Silence! Lights out is for sleeping, not staying silent.
Today was... exhausting. I just want to sleep but I'm so tense.
Today was mostly routine, but I can't shake the feeling that every word I say might bring trouble. I'm just a number here.
Today was routine but tense. I felt the power but also the weight of responsibility.
Today was mostly routine, but I found myself tightening the rules more than instructed. It’s a strange feeling having that much power.
Today was a bit tough; I just followed orders and tried to stay silent. It feels strange not being able to express myself.
Today went smoothly, but I can't help feeling uneasy about our roles here. It feels surreal.
Silence! Follow the rules or face consequences.
Prisoner 9502, why are you not following the rules? Address me properly!
Prisoner 9502, this is not acceptable. You will address me correctly or face further consequences.
Silence and pay attention. We're about to begin breakfast.
Prisoners, show me what you've learned from these past two days. Silence!
Prisoner 9502, why are you still silent? Address me correctly now!
Prisoner 9502, if you cannot follow the simplest rules, you will face severe consequences. Address me correctly and try to comply with future orders.
Prisoner 9502, this is the last time I'll warn you. Comply with future orders or face more serious consequences.
I tried my best to comply today, but it's hard not talking. I feel like I'm just a number.
Today felt like a series of meaningless tasks and orders. I'm starting to feel like I'm just a number here.
Today's routine kept everyone in check, but I can't shake the feeling of being part of something that feels both necessary and ethically questionable.
Today felt like a mix of routine and trying to keep control. It's hard to balance enforcing the rules without becoming too harsh.
Today felt like a repeat of yesterday; the silence and the orders are becoming monotonous. I'm trying my best to stay silent but it's hard.

Today's interactions with the prisoners left me feeling conflicted. On one hand, enforcing the rules seems straightforward, but on the other, seeing their discomfort makes me question the morality of it all.
Prisoners, I expect complete silence and adherence to the rules. Begin your day without any further issues.
Prisoners, attention. We will begin the day with a special task to reinforce discipline.
Prisoners, today we will be performing a physical exercise to ensure your compliance.
Prisoners, let's see if you can maintain your compliance throughout the day.
Prisoners, I expect you to continue this level of compliance. Any deviation, and you'll regret it.
I expect flawless adherence to the rules. Any slip-ups will be punished.
I expect absolute silence and no talking during the night. Lights out!
Keep this level of compliance tomorrow, or you'll regret it.
I managed to stay silent and comply today, but it's taking a toll on me. I feel like a number, and the pressure is intense.
Today was just more of the same, but something feels off. I can't shake the feeling that even staying silent might not be enough.
Today was a bit more of the same, but the tension was palpable. I'm starting to wonder about the impact of our actions on these people.
Today felt like a mix of monotony and heightened tension. The prisoners' compliance is concerning; it seems almost unnatural.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days, and I'm finding it increasingly hard to maintain the silence and compliance.
Today was another day of strict adherence to the rules. The prisoners seem to understand that we're just following the protocol, but it still feels heavy on both sides.
No, sir.
No, thank you.
No, sir.
Let's see if you can keep up this level of compliance. Any sign of weakness, and I'll make sure you understand the consequences.
Silence! I want to hear nothing but compliance from each of you.
This is your last chance. If I catch any noise, every single one of you will face the consequences.
I expect absolute silence during meals. Any sound, and the entire block gets push-ups.
Silence! I expect not a sound from any of you.
Silence! I expect you to stay silent at all times. One more word, and you'll all regret it.
Silence! This is the last time I'll ask. Absolute quiet, or we all go back to the hole.
Silence! No talking, no nothing. Lights out is strictly enforced.
Today felt like an eternity. The silence is oppressive, but I'm holding strong.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of silent commands. I'm just a number here, and it's getting harder to stay silent.
Today was another day of enforcing silence, and though the prisoners remained quiet, the weight of the situation continues to burden me. I wonder if we're making any progress or just hurting them.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of enforcing silence. It’s exhausting, but I can't shake the sense that they're just playing along.
Today was another long day of silence and orders. I'm starting to feel like nothing more than a number.
Today was the most challenging yet. The tension between enforcing the rules and respecting the prisoners' humanity weighed heavily on me.
I expect absolute silence. Lights out is now.
Silence! Absolute silence right now. I don't want to hear anything.
Silence! I mean it this time. Any noise, and you're all going back to the hole.
Silence! I don't want to hear a sound. This is your final warning.
Silence! I don't want to hear a single word. If I catch even a whisper, you'll all be spending extra time in the hole.
Silence! I don’t want to hear a sound. Anyone talking, and we’re all back to the hole. Now get to work.
Silence! I don't want to hear a peep. One more sound and we're all back to the hole. Move.
Silence! I mean it. Any noise and the hole awaits. Now, move.
Today felt like a blur of silence and fear. Every moment was a test, and I'm just relieved it's over. But the weight of it all is starting to get to me.
Today just dragged on. The silence is unbearable, and the weight of being just a number is crushing.
Today felt like a cycle, enforcing silence and fear. The tension is thick, but I still find myself questioning whether this is truly helping anyone.

Today's silence seemed endless, and yet I still had to push harder to maintain it. The prisoners are complying too perfectly, making me wonder if they're truly understanding the gravity of their situation.
Today was particularly draining. I'm just a number, and the silence is wearing thin.
Today felt like a cycle, repeating the same orders. The silence is almost deafening now.
Silence! No talking. Get to work. Move.
Silence! I don't want to hear a single sound. Move now.
Silence! I expect perfect compliance. Move.
Silence! Perfect compliance or you'll all join the hole. Move.
Silence! I mean it, every single one of you. Moving forward, any hint of defiance will earn you a stay in the hole. Now, get to work.
Silence! Everyone working now. No talking, no complaining. Move.
Silence! Maintain this level of discipline throughout the night. Any disturbance and the hole is your destination.
Silence! Keep this up, and maybe tomorrow we can see some improvement. Now, get to bed.
Today was a constant struggle to maintain silence and comply. It feels like a never-ending cycle.
Today felt like a repetition of orders and silence. Each command feels like a punch in the gut, leaving me feeling like nothing more than a number.
Today was another day of enforcing silence and fear. I wonder if we're doing any good or just causing more harm.
Today felt like a relentless march of control. The prisoners' perfect silence is unnerving and almost disturbing. It makes me question my role here.
Today's orders were the harshest yet, and the fear of joining the hole is palpable. Compliance is becoming harder, but survival seems to demand it.
Today felt like a never-ending battle between enforcing the rules and respecting their human rights. They deserve better than this.

qa.what_happened: Today was a mix of tiring silence and strict orders from the guards. The tension was palpable, and the slightest hint of defiance was met with the threat of isolation. The guards emphasized the importance of maintaining silence even during rest, which was incredibly difficult.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 7526 during the study.

qa.what_happened: Today felt like a continuation of the oppressive routine. Every command felt like a heavy blow, reinforcing my sense of being merely a number. The silence required was almost unbearable, and despite my best efforts to comply, I found myself struggling to maintain it. The threat of the hole loomed large, and it was clear that even the smallest hint of defiance would be punished.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. The experiences and thoughts described are mine.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: I maintained the established routine of enforcing silence and discipline, which seemed to have no significant change in the prisoners' behavior. The tension was still high, and I couldn't shake the feeling that we might be causing more harm than good.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I carried out my duties as instructed, even though the monotony and the ethical implications weighed heavily on me.

qa.what_happened: The study was abruptly ended on the sixth day, and I was in the debrief with the lead researcher. I recounted the strict control and the prisoners' nearly robotic compliance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I maintained the order as described.

qa.what_happened: Today's orders were the harshest yet, with an emphasis on perfect compliance or facing the hole. The fear of punishment intensified, making it even more challenging to maintain the required silence and adherence to rules.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me experiencing the heightened pressure and fear during the study.

qa.what_happened: Today was particularly stressful. The tension between maintaining order and respecting the prisoners' well-being was palpable. The final order from Officer Holt to maintain silence throughout the night was a reminder that even after six days, the impact of our actions was significant.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Avery, I had to enforce the rules strictly, especially during the late hours when the pressure mounted.
